# A mean-preserving torque target need not have factor-two cap domination

This is an exact obstruction for the proposed n=1 torque reduction. The
actual mixed centroid has integer base. The obstruction holds for every
choice of torque coupling because the tested cap contains the entire
output fiber. It does not disprove conditional OC.

## 1. The concrete convex body

Let

    C={(z,x):0<=z<=25, 0<=x<=25-z} subset R x R.

This triangle is a convex body. Its positive integer fibers are the
intervals [0,25-z] at z=0,...,24. The fiber at z=25 is a point and has
zero relevant one-dimensional volume. Thus

    M=sum_(r=1)^25 r=325,
    sum_z z(25-z)=8M,
    sum_z integral_0^(25-z) x dx
       =(1/2)sum_(r=1)^25 r^2=5525/2.

The actual mixed centroid is

    g=(8,17/2),

which belongs to its fiber [0,17]. The closed ambient halfspace

    H={z>=8}

contains the centroid and the entire centroid fiber. Its mixed mass is

    mu(H)=sum_(r=1)^17 r=153.

Any noncentral torque target preserving the total noncentral mass and
supported in the centroid fiber has mass

    nu(H)=M-|K_8|=325-17=308>306=2mu(H).                (1)

Adding the original centroid-fiber measure gives a mass-325 target
rho, and rho(H)=325>306 as well. Thus neither target can satisfy the
universal cap domination nu(H)<=2mu(H) or rho(H)<=2mu(H), even when only
caps containing the actual centroid are tested.

## 2. The general integer family

More generally let N=3k+1 and use the triangle 0<=z<=N,
0<=x<=N-z. Its mixed base centroid is k, because

    M=N(N+1)/2,
    sum_z z(N-z)/M=(N-1)/3=k.

The centroid fiber has length 2k+1. The cap z>=k has mass
(2k+1)(k+1). Hence its noncentral-target excess over twice the cap mass is

    [M-(2k+1)]-2(2k+1)(k+1)
       =(k^2-7k-4)/2.

This is positive for every integer k>=8. The concrete example above
uses k=8, for which the excess is exactly 2.

## 3. Exact torque identities, and the limited conclusion

After shifting the base centroid to 0, write negative indices as -i and
positive ones as j, with i,j>=1. Integer-centroid balance gives equal
masses to the torque measures i mu_-i and j mu_j. For any coupling pi of
these torque measures define

    T(x,y)=(j x+i y)/(i+j),
    w(i,j)=1/i+1/j,
    nu=T#(w pi),

placing the target at base 0. Convexity puts every T in K_0. Its total
mass is exactly the noncentral mixed mass, and

    w T=x/i+y/j

shows that its continuous first moment is the sum of the original
noncentral first moments. Thus the torque reduction does preserve mass
and the continuous centroid exactly. Formula (1) refutes the additional
factor-two cap domination, not these identities or target membership.

A valid extension would need a more refined relation that tracks integer
halfspace mass, adds contributions from other output fibers, or uses the
actual cap fraction of the target instead of asserting universal
factor-two domination. The inequality (1) is not a counterexample to the
conditional centroid OC target gamma_1/2=1/4.
